title: Phayao With Kids: 3-Day Family Itinerary, Thailand | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: An easy 3-day Phayao family itinerary in northern Thailand. Boat to the lake temple at Kwan Phayao, feed the fish, riverside playground, Wat Sri Khom Kham and Wat Analayo — planned day by day with short, kid-friendly drives.
keywords: Phayao family trip, Phayao with kids, Kwan Phayao boat ride, Wat Tilok Aram, Phayao itinerary
h1:
Phayao With Kids
An Easy 3-Day, 2-Night Family Trip
intro: Phayao is a small town you can take slowly with the whole family. The distances between sights are short, so you never have to rush and the kids don't get worn out. The highlight is Kwan Phayao, the largest freshwater lake in northern Thailand, where you can take a boat out to a temple in the middle of the water, feed the fish, let the kids loose in a lakeside park, and visit the pretty temples around town. We've put together a smooth 3-day plan built around actually travelling with children.

blocks.html: The nice thing about Phayao with kids is that everything sits close together. The town wraps around Kwan Phayao, and driving from one spot to the next is usually no more than 15–20 minutes. The only longer drives are the day you head out to Chiang Kham or up to the hilltop temple. In this plan we keep the first two days in town around the lake, then save the longer trips — or a quick temple stop — for the last day before you leave. Swap things around to suit your kids' ages.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Kwan Phayao, a boat ride and feeding the fish

blocks.html: The first day stays by the lake the whole time. The kids get a boat ride, get to feed the fish, and have room to run around in the park. It's a low-effort day but the most fun one for little ones.

items.activity: Stroll along Kwan Phayao and feed the fish
items.note: There's a long walking path right along the water, and the lake is full of fish. Buy bread or fish food from the vendors near the pier — this is the part the kids love most.

items.activity: Take a rowing boat to Wat Tilok Aram, the temple in the lake
items.note: Boats start at 30 THB per person (about 5 people per boat), or charter a whole boat for 150 THB that seats around 10–20. The round trip takes about an hour and you get to pay respects to the stone Buddha out in the lake. With small kids, put a life jacket on them and hold their hands getting on and off the boat.

Popular spots like Niyom Suk and Chitlom Chom Kwan have both air-conditioned rooms and waterside seating. Fried tilapia, gaeng hang lay, and nam prik num are all on the menu, and kids can eat fine if you order it without chilli.

A public park right on the lake, across from the King Ngam Mueang Monument, with a playground, a wide lawn, and a pond — plenty of space to let the kids run. Inside there's also TK Park Phayao, a cool air-conditioned children's library that's perfect for getting out of the afternoon sun.

items.activity: Watch the sunset over the lake
items.note: The evening light is lovely as the sky changes colour over the water. Settle into a lakeside café or restaurant and watch the sun go down at your own pace.

blocks.title: About the boats with small kids
blocks.html: The boat out to Wat Tilok Aram is an open rowing boat. If you're travelling with kids under five, ask the boatman for a child-sized life jacket first, and chartering your own boat is more comfortable than sharing. On full-moon holy days there's an evening candle-procession ceremony out on the water — it's lovely but busy, so skip that day if you'd rather avoid the crowds.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Wat Sri Khom Kham, Wat Analayo and a café with animals

blocks.html: Day two is a temple-and-views day, broken up with a café where the kids can meet some animals. There isn't much walking, and there are plenty of spots to sit and rest along the way.

items.activity: Wat Sri Khom Kham, home of Phra Chao Ton Luang
items.note: Phayao's main temple, right on the lake, houses Phra Chao Ton Luang — a Chiang Saen-style Buddha image with a lap 14 metres wide. The kids get to see a genuinely huge Buddha, and the temple grounds are shady and easy to walk.

items.activity: Wat Analayo Thipayaram on Doi Busarakham
items.note: A temple on a hilltop you can drive all the way up to, with several Buddha images, an Indian-style chedi, and a high viewpoint that takes in the whole lake. The road up is winding, so bring medicine if your kids get carsick.
Try khanom jeen nam ngiao at a place in town — it's mild and easy for kids — or head back to a lakeside restaurant for round two.

items.activity: Bunny Moon Café, a rabbit café by the lake
items.note: A lakeside café with a small-animal zone — rabbits, goats, and silkie chickens. The kids get to feed them and take photos while the grown-ups sip coffee with a lake view.

items.activity: Cycle or stroll along the lake in the evening
items.note: There are bikes for rent along the lake, perfect for a breezy ride beside the water. Older kids can ride their own; little ones can sit behind or ride in a samlor (pedal trishaw).

items.name: TK Park Phayao
items.blurb: A learning park inside Somdet Ya Park with a cool air-conditioned children's library and an activity zone — great for getting out of the sun or for a rainy day.

items.name: Bunny Moon Café
items.blurb: A lakeside café with rabbits, goats, and silkie chickens that kids can feed and get up close to.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Your choice: head out far, or keep it easy before you leave

blocks.html: The last day depends on how the kids are holding up. If they're still game and you want a taste of Tai Yai and Tai Lue culture, head out to Chiang Kham. If you'd rather keep things gentle before packing up, do another loop of the lake and then make your way home.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Option A · Chiang Kham — Tai Lue

items.activity: Drive out to Chiang Kham district
items.note: It's about 75 km from Phayao town, roughly an hour and a half, with rice fields and mountains along both sides of the road.

items.activity: Wat Nantaram, a Tai Yai golden-teak hall
items.note: The whole hall is built of teak and nearly a hundred years old, with finely carved detailing. There's a small antiques museum inside the temple where kids can look at old objects, and the atmosphere is quiet and easy to wander.
Try Tai Lue dishes in Chiang Kham — grilled fish and jin sam phrik — in an old wooden house, and pick up some Tai Lue stories along with the meal.
On the way back, stop at a local market for crispy pork rinds and sai ua (northern sausage) to take home.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Option B · an easy day around town

items.note: Wander the morning market, try hot sticky rice and local sweets, and feed the fish by the lake one more time.

items.activity: A late breakfast at a lakeside café
items.note: Sit at a café with a lake view and order bingsu or pastries for the kids, with one last coffee for the grown-ups.

items.activity: Pack up and take one last walk around the lake
items.note: Get a family photo by the lake before you go — the King Ngam Mueang Monument is a good spot for it.

blocks.text: Tips for a smooth Phayao trip with kids

items: Stay on or near the lake — you can wake up, feed the fish, and stroll by the water without a long drive every morning.
Mornings and evenings have the best weather — the midday sun is strong, so plan outdoor activities for early and late, and retreat to a café or TK Park in the afternoon.
Bring warm layers in the cool season — from November to February it gets chilly by the lake and up on the hill, and little ones will need an extra layer.
Pack motion-sickness medicine for Wat Analayo and the Chiang Kham trip — both the road up the hill and the road to Chiang Kham are winding.
Carry cash — boat fares, roadside snacks, and lots of small shops are easier to pay in cash.

blocks.title: How many days?
blocks.html: If you have very young kids, 2 days and 1 night is enough — focus on the lake and Wat Sri Khom Kham and skip the longer trips. But if you want the lake, the hilltop temple, and the Tai Lue culture in Chiang Kham, 3 days and 2 nights is just right and won't be rushed enough to leave the kids cranky.

faq.q: Can I take small kids on the boat to Wat Tilok Aram?
faq.a: Yes. It's a short rowing-boat crossing of the lake, about an hour round trip. Fares start at 30 THB per person, or 150 THB to charter the whole boat. We'd suggest asking the boatman for a child-sized life jacket, and chartering your own boat is more comfortable and safer than sharing.

faq.q: How many days do I need in Phayao with the family?
faq.a: With very young kids, 2 days and 1 night is plenty — focus on the lake and Wat Sri Khom Kham. If you want the full set — the boat ride, Wat Analayo on the hill, and Tai Lue culture in Chiang Kham — 3 days and 2 nights is just right. The distances in town are short, so the kids won't get too tired.

faq.q: Are there things to do for kids in Phayao?
faq.a: Yes. Somdet Ya 90th Anniversary Park on the lake has a playground and TK Park Phayao, a learning park. Bunny Moon Café has rabbits, goats, and silkie chickens that kids can see and feed, and feeding the fish along the lake is always a hit with children too.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Phayao with kids?
faq.a: The cool season, November to February, has comfortable weather, clear skies, and lovely lake views — though it gets chilly by the lake and on the hill, so pack warm clothes for the kids. If you come in the rainy or hot season, plan outdoor activities for morning and evening and retreat from the sun into a café or library in the afternoon.

faq.q: What can kids eat in Phayao?
faq.a: The lakeside restaurants have fried tilapia, clear soups, and fried rice that are easy for kids — just order without chilli. Northern dishes like nam ngiao or gaeng hang lay aren't too spicy if you ask for them mild. The lakeside cafés also have bingsu, pastries, and cold milk for the kids.
